title: Two beam segments joined by a hinge: condensed stiffness coefficients

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.location: Example 4.14 (stiffness matrix of the combined member)
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. The source derives symbolically the stiffness matrix of a member 1-0-2 with a moment hinge at 0 (segments a and b, equal EI). Numeric instance chosen here: a = 4 m, b = 2 m, E = 200 kN/mm^2, I = 200e6 mm^4. Model: members n1-h and h-n2, the hinge as a full rz release at end j of the first member; both end nodes fully held. Combination V imposes v1 = 1 mm, combination R imposes theta1 = 0.001 rad; the reactions at n1 and n2 are the first and second column of the printed matrix times the imposed displacement. First order, no shear deformation. Section properties the source does not give because they do not enter its plane model (Iy, J; A where stated) are placeholders that do not influence the targets.
